messages.text: Djokovic out of ATP Finals race after shock Paris exit along with No 1 Zverev

metadata.summary: For just the second time in 20 seasons, Novak Djokovic has failed to qualify for the season-ending ATP Finals after a shock defeat in the second round of the Rolex Paris Masters.
metadata.content: ATP Paris Masters: Novak Djokovic eliminated from ATP Finals race as world No 1 Alexander Zverev also suffers shock exit | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content ATP Paris Masters: Novak Djokovic eliminated from ATP Finals race as world No 1 Alexander Zverev also suffers shock exit Novak Djokovic fails to qualify for season-ending ATP Finals after shock defeat in French capital, while world No 1 Alexander Zverev also exits Paris Masters; You can watch the ATP Paris Masters live on Sky Sports this week Wednesday 4 November 2026 17:51, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Novak Djokovic against Rinky Hijikata from the Paris Masters For just the second time in 20 seasons, Novak Djokovic has failed to qualify for the season-ending ATP Finals after a shock defeat in the second round of the Rolex Paris Masters. The 39-year-old, who also failed to make the 2017 edition due to a elbow injury, needed a run to the semi-finals to keep himself in with a chance of clinching a spot at the season-ending showpiece in Turin. Djokovic, a seven-time champion in Paris, started well against 25-year-old Australian Rinky Hijikata, the world No 83, but faded badly in a 2-6 6-3 6-3 defeat. messages.text: Leicestershire's relegation confirmed as points deduction for 'poor' pitch stands

metadata.summary: Leicestershire's relegation to County Championship Division Two has been confirmed after the club's points deduction for breaching pitch regulations was upheld.
metadata.content: Leicestershire's County Championship relegation confirmed as points deduction for 'poor' pitch upheld | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Leicestershire's County Championship relegation confirmed as points deduction for 'poor' pitch upheld Leicestershire join Hampshire in being relegated from Division One; Foxes argued that state of pitch for victory over Glamorgan had been due to shooting of Bollywood film days before fixture; Leicestershire finish 17 points behind third-bottom Essex in table as 19-point sanction stands Wednesday 4 November 2026 16:46, UK Image: Leicestershire's relegation to County Championship Division Two has been confirmed after the club's points deduction for breaching pitch regulations was upheld Leicestershire's relegation to County Championship Division Two has been confirmed after the club's points deduction for breaching pitch regulations was upheld. The Foxes were hit with a 27-point penalty, later cut to 19, after the surface at Grace Road was rated "poor" by the match referee following the win over Glamorgan in August. Leicestershire, who argued the state of the pitch was due to the unscheduled shooting of a Bollywood film days before the Glamorgan fixture, had eight points from the original punishment of 27 reinstated but then appealed against the 19-point sanction. metadata.summary: Michael Atherton sees no issue with Lancashire's handling of James Anderson's release from the county - but would have been tempted to hand the veteran seam bowler a new contract.
metadata.content: James Anderson: Michael Atherton says Lancashire did not handle bowler's release badly - but should they have extended his contract? | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Opinion James Anderson: Michael Atherton says Lancashire did not handle bowler's release badly - but should they have extended his contract? Where could James Anderson end up next after release from boyhood club Lancashire? Sky Sports Cricket pundit Michael Atherton does not believe Old Trafford county handled Anderson's exit badly, saying director of cricket Paul Farbrace did not "hide behind the decision" Michael Atherton Cricket expert and columnist Wednesday 4 November 2026 15:09, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch Jimmy Anderson's final wicket for Lancashire back in September, against Kent in the County Championship Michael Atherton sees no issue with Lancashire's handling of James Anderson's release from the county - but would have been tempted to hand the veteran seam bowler a new contract. Anderson, 44, bagged 50 wickets at an average of 17.68 in the County Championship during a 2026 season in which Lancashire finished second bottom of Division Two under his captaincy. Anderson was informed in a meeting with the Red Rose hierarchy that he would not be offered a new deal at a county he first represented in a first-class match in 2002, with new director of cricket Paul Farbrace wanting to build an attack for the future. metadata.summary: Jesus Owono says he is going through the most difficult ‌days of his life in a statement released by his club FC Andorra on Wednesday, following the death of ‌Tenerife forward Jesus De Miguel.
metadata.content: Jesus de Miguel: Goalkeeper Jesus Owono experiencing 'most difficult days of my life' after Tenerife forward's death following collision | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Jesus de Miguel: Goalkeeper Jesus Owono experiencing 'most difficult days of my life' after Tenerife forward's death following collision Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel died after a collision with FC Andorra's goalkeeper Jesus Owono, who has now released a statement; Lautaro Spatz also took to Instagram to defend his team-mate, who has deleted his account on the social media platform Wednesday 4 November 2026 17:09, UK Image: Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono walks off the pitch after he collided with FC Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel Jesus Owono says he is going through the most difficult ‌days of his life in a statement released by his club FC Andorra on Wednesday, following the death of ‌Tenerife forward Jesus De Miguel. The Tenerife forward died on Tuesday morning following a collision with Owono during a Spanish second division match on Monday. Owono was sent off for the clash having raced from his goal and struck 30-year-old De Miguel at force, with the Tenerife player subsequently suffering a cardiac arrest after being taken into intensive care. "These are the most difficult days of my life," ‌Owono said in a statement. "I struggle to find the words, and I find it very hard to ​process what has happened. messages.text: Wilder to fight Opetaia on Fury vs Joshua undercard

metadata.summary: Deontay Wilder will fight Jai Opetaia on the undercard of Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff on December 11.
metadata.content: Fury vs Joshua undercard: Deontay Wilder to fight Jai Opetaia in heavyweight bout on December 11 Principality Stadium bill | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Fury vs Joshua undercard: Deontay Wilder to fight Jai Opetaia in heavyweight bout on December 11 Principality Stadium bill Deontay Wilder and cruiserweight star Jai Opetaia will collide on the undercard of the Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua all-British mega-fight on December 11 at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff; Opetaia, unbeaten at 200lbs, will take on a ferocious puncher in his first bout in the division Wednesday 4 November 2026 16:10, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Back in 2017 Deontay Wilder had to be restrained by the referee after he floored Bermane Stiverne three times in a dramatic first round. Deontay Wilder will fight Jai Opetaia on the undercard of Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff on December 11. Unbeaten cruiserweight star Opetaia is stepping up to heavyweight for the first time to box Wilder, a former world champion and renowned as one of the hardest punchers ever in the sport. In the main event, Fury and Joshua meet in a long-awaited all-British heavyweight fight. It would be a first high-level heavyweight fight for Opetaia, a previous holder of the IBF championship who has been a force at cruiserweight.
